title: Interpretation, Model and Validity
quickIdea: An interpretation fixes a domain and a truth value for every predicate on it. A sentence is valid when every interpretation makes it true, satisfiable when at least one does, and a model is an interpretation that does make it true.
remember: An interpretation is a non-empty domain plus, for every predicate symbol, which tuples of elements satisfy it.
A model of a sentence is an interpretation in which the sentence is true; a countermodel is one in which it is false.
Valid (logically true): true in every interpretation. Unsatisfiable: true in none. Satisfiable but not valid: true in some, false in others.
Validity is a property of closed formulas; a formula with free variables is evaluated only after an assignment to those variables.
First-order validity quantifies over all interpretations, not over the rows of one truth table, which is why a propositional truth table cannot settle a first-order question.
One countermodel is enough to show a formula is not valid; showing validity needs an argument that covers every domain.
A formula is valid exactly when its negation is unsatisfiable.

example.prompt: Is for all x P(x) implies there exists x P(x) valid?
example.work: Domains in first-order logic are non-empty. If P holds for every element then some element satisfies it.
example.answer: Valid over every non-empty domain. Over an empty domain the implication would also hold vacuously, which is why some texts avoid empty domains altogether.

gateAngle: GATE CS 2016 Set 2 Q.27 asks which formula is NOT valid; one countermodel settles it - domain the natural numbers, p(x) 'x is even', q(x) 'x is odd', so every number is one or the other but not all are even and not all are odd.

variations.label: CONCEPTUAL PRACTICE QUESTION
variations.question: Is for all x P(x) satisfiable? Is it valid?
variations.why: Take a non-empty domain with P true everywhere: true. Take P false at one element: false. So it is true in some interpretations and false in others.

variations.label: ORIGINAL PYQ-STYLE QUESTION
variations.question: Give an interpretation in which there exists x P(x) is false.
variations.answer: Any non-empty domain with P empty, for example {1} with P(1) false.
variations.why: The existential is false exactly when no element satisfies P.

trap.what: Declaring a formula false because it fails in the one interpretation you happened to try, or true because it held in a few.
trap.why: Validity is about every interpretation; satisfiability is about at least one. The two questions are different and the same example answers only one of them.
trap.counterexample: For all x there exists y (y < x) is true over the integers but false over the natural numbers, so it is satisfiable and not valid.

check.question: A sentence is false in exactly one interpretation and true in all others. Is it valid?
check.explanation: Valid means true in every interpretation; one countermodel is enough to deny validity. It is still satisfiable, because it is true in the others.
